text: At ten I found two men with Holmes, Peter Jones of Scotland Yard and Mister Merryweather, a director of the bank. <break time="0.8s" /> We went down into the banks huge cellar, where thirty thousand gold coins from the Bank of France were stored in boxes. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes covered our lantern, and we waited in complete darkness for more than an hour without making a sound. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly a stone in the floor began to rise, and a white hand appeared, followed by a clean, boyish face. <break time="0.8s" /> The man climbed out quickly, but Holmes seized him at once, and although his partner escaped down the hole, police officers caught him at Wilsons door. <break time="0.8s" /> Later Holmes explained that the League had been invented only to get Wilson out of his shop for four hours a day. <break time="0.8s" /> His assistant, who was really the famous criminal John Clay, had used those hours to dig a tunnel to the bank. <break time="0.8s" /> They closed the League because the tunnel was finished, and they chose Saturday because the bank would stay shut until Monday. <break time="0.8s" /> I thought that if Holmes had not noticed such small clues, the gold would have disappeared long before Monday morning. <break time="0.8s" /> You are a benefactor of the human race, I said, but Holmes only shrugged and said that the work was everything to him.
